root_causes.root_cause: RFC-027 D7 dynamic timeout scaling was implemented as dead code: chunked_docling_timeout_s() exists in converters.py but is never imported or called by worker.py. The worker always uses fixed CHILD_TIMEOUT=1770s (29.5min). world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf (292 pages, 6.4MB) requires 24-49 min for Docling conversion at 5-10s/page on CPU. With 2 chunks of ~150 pages each, total processing can exceed the fixed 1770s timeout, causing the worker to SIGTERM/SIGKILL the child subprocess before any artifacts are persisted.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Wire chunked_docling_timeout_s into _run_converter_subprocess: (1) accept an optional timeout_override parameter in _run_converter_subprocess, (2) in converters_cli, after chunked conversion, emit chunk_count in the stdout JSON, (3) OR pre-compute the expected timeout in the worker before spawning the child by reading the page count from the staged file. Simplest approach: have converters_cli emit the dynamic timeout as part of a pre-flight page-count check, or increase CHILD_TIMEOUT to accommodate the chunked path (e.g. 3600s) and let JOB_TIMEOUT follow.
